changes_vs_current: New topic. Scope: comedians and comedic performers. Excluded: primary late-night/talk hosts (Fallon, Kimmel, Carson, Leno, Letterman, Colbert, Stewart, Conan, Noah) and pure screen actors (DeVito, Jack Black, Jamie Foxx, Seth Rogen, Chaplin, Leslie Nielsen, Steve Carell). Raw order by average position across the 6 people sources: 1 Robin Williams, 2 Jim Carrey, 3 Eddie Murphy, 4 Adam Sandler, 5 Bill Murray, 6 Steve Martin, 7 Will Ferrell, 8 Kevin Hart, 9 Tim Allen, 10 Steve Harvey, 11 Lucille Ball, 12 Richard Pryor, 13 Carol Burnett, 14 Dave Chappelle, 15 Tina Fey, 16 Whoopi Goldberg, 17 Chris Rock, 18 Jerry Seinfeld, 19 Bernie Mac, 20 John Candy, 21 Bill Cosby, 22 Mike Myers, 23 Chris Farley, 24 Dan Aykroyd (25 Chevy Chase, ... 34 George Carlin). Gut-check moves (the general-fame sources favor broad celebrity over 'comedian' recall, and none of them measures comedian naming lower): Dave Chappelle 14->8 (Pollstar #2, OnBuy #7, RS #9; YouGov fame 89%); Jerry Seinfeld 18->9 (Pollstar #3, RS #7; fame 89%); Richard Pryor 12->10 (Ranker #8, OnBuy #10, #1 on both critic lists); George Carlin 34->11 (Ranker #4 of 452k votes, #2 on both critic lists; his low YouGov fame of 76% reflects his era, not recall); Chris Rock 17->12 (OnBuy #15, YouGov fame 91%, #5 on both critic lists). Knock-on effects: Bill Murray 5->13 (pushed out of the top 12 by the gut-check items; still Ranker #3 and YouGov popularity #4); Steve Martin 6->5, Will Ferrell 7->6, Kevin Hart 8->7; Tim Allen/Steve Harvey/Lucille Ball/Carol Burnett/Tina Fey/Whoopi/Bernie Mac/John Candy/Bill Cosby/Mike Myers/Chris Farley each drop 4-6 places to 14-24; Dan Aykroyd (raw 24) drops off. Editorial: Bill Cosby (data #22) left off the public board; Mike Myers and Chris Farley move up to 22-23 and Dan Aykroyd (next in the data, raw #24) takes #24.
confidence: medium: the top 12 is well supported (YouGov popularity and fame plus Ranker, OnBuy, Pollstar and critic lists all agree), but no US poll asks 'name a comedian'. Positions 13-24 rest mainly on YouGov and Wikipedia general-fame data, which favors sitcom and film comedic actors (Tim Allen, Lucille Ball, John Candy, Mike Myers, Chris Farley) over stand-ups people may type (Martin Lawrence, Joan Rivers, Rodney Dangerfield, Ellen DeGeneres, Jeff Foxworthy, Gabriel Iglesias).
